basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models a governed territorial unit with legal or statistical standing, unlike a settlement or place that is a named locality.
Keeps boundary assertions per source, so official, statistical, claimed and de facto lines can coexist for one unit.
Separates the unit from the government that administers it and from the jurisdiction whose law applies there.
Treats codes such as ISO 3166-2 or NUTS as versioned bindings, not as the identity of the unit itself.

may: Validate boundary geometry, topology and CRS and report gaps or overlaps.
Resolve a unit by code or name for a stated date and code system.
Propose a territorial change with its source instrument for authority review.
Issue a purpose-bound view at the minimum precision the use needs.
mustNot: Change canonical unit identity, level or legal-effect state without register authority.
Present one claimed or disputed boundary as the universally recognised line.
Infer current administrative identity from a code, name or population figure alone.
Reuse a retired or reassigned code as if it still named the old unit.
Suppress a recorded dispute or recognition assertion from a view that requests it.
requiresHuman: Registering a merger, split, abolition or reclassification of a unit.
Recording or publishing a recognition or dispute position on a contested boundary.
Releasing sensitive boundary or authority data beyond its granted audience.

considerations: Boundary representations in disputed regions carry political weight and can harm people on either side if presented as settled.
Unit boundaries decide access to services, voting and taxation, so errors shift rights between residents.
Historic units must remain resolvable so that old records about people and land keep their meaning.
affectedParties: Communities in disputed or recently changed territories

items: An administrative area has an issuing register, a unit type and level, codes, official names and an effective period.
It is often confused with a settlement, postal zone, electoral district or statistical grid cell that shares its name.
Outdated boundaries route emergency services or benefits to the wrong authority.
Code reuse after reorganisation silently merges histories of different units.
Coordinate reference system mismatch shifts boundaries and misassigns parcels or addresses.
Publishing contested lines as official provokes diplomatic or community conflict.
UN M49 standard country or area codes for statistical use.
OGC Simple Features and GeoJSON (IETF RFC 7946) for boundary geometry.
Area in square kilometres, computed on a stated equal-area projection.
Boundary length in kilometres, with the source scale or resolution stated.
Positional accuracy of boundary vertices in metres, against a stated reference survey.
Coordinate reference system and epoch of the boundary geometry.
